correctness.rationale: For four affinely independent integer-cube sites, the squared point-to-closed-triangle distance is exactly the perpendicular-plane determinant quotient when its barycentric foot is feasible, or the minimum of three rational segment distances otherwise. The supplied standard-library verifier enumerates all marked unordered-triangle configurations once (58,528), compares every one against an independent seven-KKT-support convex minimum, and checks the 88-row full spectrum and 48-element cube-isometry orbit keys. Exact arithmetic proves a complete finite classification, not an extrapolated infinite claim. At level 1/29: 48 in one orbit; next 1/21: 96 in two orbits; third 1/17: 24 in one orbit. All representative vertices are directly included in the replayable script.

originality.rationale: The full original papers establish the first minimal level and its unique orbit, or global minima in larger competing face types. They do not provide the all-distance distribution in the marked 3x3x3 lattice tetrahedron model, the nonminimal sharp threshold 1/sqrt(21), or its two equality orbits. Comprehensive statement-level comparisons and actual indexed searches support a provisional same-model originality PASS, subject to residual unindexed-equivalence risk.
residual_risks: An older finite small-lattice-cube dataset or supplementary program might implicitly contain the same 88-level distribution but be absent from searched indexes; negative search results do not rule this out.
The source theorem already gives the first minimizer and its uniqueness; only second-rank isolation, second-rank orbit classification, and the complete frequency distribution are assessed as new.
The finite theorem does not establish an all-k stability gap; publication or independent assessment could judge its scientific importance differently.

value.rationale: The value is the entire exact distribution of a motivated flatness/facial-separation invariant on the first genuinely nonbinary three-dimensional lattice cube, rather than an arbitrary small slice. It supplies 88 rational masses on all 58,528 marked tetrahedra, the next sharp positive isolation gap above the known unique extremizer, and two distinct geometric runner-up orbits. Such exact data provide a self-contained finite benchmark for separating numerical face-distance and affine-hull calculations. The result deliberately does not claim a larger-cube theorem or generic algorithm speedup.
